data.raw_text:
🇺🇦🇺🇸 Tested in the Black Sea
Now It’s the Turn of the Chinese Coast

The "Balikatan-2026" exercise - recently launched in the Philippines and led by U.S. forces - has provided plenty of talking points, ranging from the sheer scale of this year's event to the fact that U.S. Special Operations Forces (SOF) deployed their new unmanned surface vessel (USV).

Any Russian observer who has been following the Special Military Operation (SMO) for the past five years will surely notice that the unmanned boat - presented as a product of the company Red Cat - is, in fact, a copy of the Ukrainian *Magura* USV.

As part of the exercise, SOF units practiced launching the maritime platform into the water and subsequently tested it as a "fire-ship" style USV, simulating an attack on a vessel in the South China Sea. Targeting guidance for the operation was provided by a new reconnaissance UAV developed by Anduril.

And this is a completely predictable turn of events: Ukrainian technologies - particularly drones - emerged largely thanks to funding and technical expertise provided by Western nations. These nations supplied the equipment to the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) for operational testing; subsequently, the most effective systems are being adopted by all member states of the Alliance.

❗️The specific focus on U.S. SOF is also intentional: they are the key operators of such systems. This applies both to analogues of the *Geran* drones - such as LUCAS, which were tested against Iran - and to the USVs that are set to be actively deployed to counter China.

As for the Ukrainian claims that the Americans "stole" their designs - in this context, such arguments are utterly nonsensical. Anything utilized by the AFU that proves effective will, sooner or later, be re-branded as someone else's proprietary technology - something that was merely field-tested in Ukraine using the AFU as proxies.

rybar
